answer: One concrete mechanism: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because beacon only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, kernel is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any lagoon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
